title: Fit a Mini-ITX server board into a 1U chassis, flat on its four standoffs with its connectors through the I/O shield
instruction: Fit the server board into the chassis, seated on its four standoffs with its connectors through the I/O shield, and let go of it.
context: Robots that build and repair servers would speed up the build-out of AI computing. System integrators and data-centre technicians assemble compact 1U servers such as the Supermicro SYS-5019A-FTN4 on a bench from a Mini-ITX board (A2SDi-8C-HLN4F) and a CSE-505-203B chassis. The board's rear connectors must pass through the chassis's I/O shield and its mounting holes must sit over the four standoffs before it can be screwed down.
setup: Units: metres; x forward from the line through the two YAM arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the bench top is z 0.7475; the arm bases are at y +0.305 and -0.305. The layout matches the screenshot (lot A). (1) Chassis, fixed (in the real trial it sits against bench stops at its rear and left faces, fixture/README.md): a Supermicro CSE-505-203B 1U chassis base, lid off, front toward the robot, outer faces x 0.199 to 0.448 (249 mm deep) and y -0.291 to +0.146 (437 mm wide), 1 mm steel floor and walls, walls 43 mm high. Four brass M3 standoffs (5.5 mm across, 6.35 mm high, estimates) stand on the floor at the Mini-ITX mounting-hole pattern (holes C, F, H, J: 154.94 mm and 132.08 mm apart front to back, 157.48 mm apart side to side), centred on the seated board at x 0.360, y 0.050; their tops are at z 0.7549. The rear wall's window holds a 1 mm steel I/O shield (inner face x 0.447) for the board, with five rectangular cut-outs: two 17.9 x 9.4 mm for the D-sub connector shells (0.45 mm clearance each side), one 18 x 32 mm for the network jack over two USB ports and two 18 x 29 mm for the network-jack pairs (1 mm clearance each side; cut-out sizes are estimates). Inside the chassis: the power supply (150 x 82 x 40.5 mm) at the rear right (x 0.297 to 0.447, y -0.180 to -0.099), a 40 mm fan holder (28 x 40 x 40 mm) ahead of the board's place (x 0.205 to 0.233, y 0.030 to 0.070) and a 2.5 in drive bracket (100 x 70 x 12 mm) at the front right. (2) A black conductive-foam pad, 150 x 150 x 10 mm, fixed to the bench left of the chassis, centred at x 0.272, y 0.330. (3) The board, loose on the pad, components up: a Supermicro A2SDi-8C-HLN4F Mini-ITX server board (170 x 170 x 1.6 mm, 0.45 kg with its heat sink, estimate) with its passive heat sink (60 x 60 x 24 mm, estimate) 10 mm from the board's centre toward the front, four DIMM slots, and along its rear edge, from right to left seen from the front: a VGA D-sub, a network jack over two USB ports (16 x 30 mm), two stacked pairs of network jacks (16 x 27 mm each) and a COM D-sub (positions along the edge are estimates). Each D-sub has a 31 x 12.5 mm zinc flange 2 mm past the PCB edge and a 17 x 8.5 mm shell 6 mm in front of the flange; the jacks overhang the edge by 4 mm. Lot A: the board's centre at x 0.272, y 0.330, its connector edge facing away from the robot (+x). Lot B: the board's centre at x 0.284, y 0.338, turned so its connector edge faces the chassis (-y). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read at the end of each trial; trials are run on lots A and B and averaged. Zero first: 0 at any moment, and it stays 0 for the rest of the trial, if the board moves downward faster than 0.6 m/s (a drop or a slam, about the speed of a 2 cm fall; judged from the video), if any corner of the board comes within 3 mm of the chassis floor (it slipped off the standoffs) or if it leaves the bench. Every credited level also needs all of: the robot has let go (no part of either arm's links 3 to 5, gripper or fingertips within 5 mm of the board), the board has then stayed still for 1 s, and it lies flat on all four standoffs in its place: the gap under it at each standoff at most 1 mm (a 1 mm feeler gauge does not enter), every standoff top fully under the PCB (seen from above, none shows past the PCB edge), tilt at most 2 degrees (phone inclinometer on the PCB), connector edge toward the shield and turned at most 5 degrees from square to the rear wall (protractor), and every mounting hole within 10 mm of its standoff (ruler). Levels: 1.0 when the board is home: both D-sub flanges bear on the shield's inner face (gap at most 0.3 mm, checked with a 0.3 mm feeler gauge) and an M3 screw starts by hand in every mounting hole without moving the board (hole axis within 0.48 mm of its standoff's); 0.5 when both D-sub shells have entered their cut-outs at least 1 mm (flush with or past the 1 mm shield's outer face: a straightedge laid on the outer face touches each shell) but the board is not home; 0.25 when the board lies flat on its standoffs as above but a D-sub shell is less than 1 mm into its cut-out; 0 otherwise (left on the pad, still held, tilted, turned round, off its place). The whole-trial record is cleared only by a scene reset (the board back at its start, at rest, after a jump of over 20 mm in one control step).
run_limit: 1,200 control steps per trial (60 seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: 1. Lift the board out of the chassis by its edges (ESD wrist strap and gloves). 2. Lot A: lay it flat on the foam pad, components up, centred at x 0.272, y 0.330, connector edge facing away from the robot. Lot B: centred at x 0.284, y 0.338, connector edge facing the chassis. Use the pad's corner marks and a ruler. 3. Check that the shield, standoffs and chassis are undisturbed and the chassis sits against its two bench stops (rear and left) (fixture/README.md).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size, PhysX 240 Hz. Board, heat sink and connectors are one rigid body of boxes; connector positions, heat sink size and the 0.45 kg mass are estimates. The PCB has no hole geometry: the 5.5 mm standoff tops are wider than its 3.96 mm holes, so it rests on them as the real board does. Shield cut-outs are plain rectangles, no EMI fingers. Friction 0.45/0.35 (estimate). Chassis interior parts are boxes at estimated sizes and positions. Two lots stop one fixed habit.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; both trials ran to the 1,200-step limit); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (full score at step 533)
